te: Representatives sent to consider the Thai traditional medicine bill, 2 bills studied in advance, and 6 complaints about the police
se: Meeting on Wednesday, 28 October 2026, at 13.00, Meeting Room 401, Floor 4, Parliament House. The meeting resolved to send representatives from the committee's share to serve on the ad hoc committee considering the Protection and Promotion of Thai Traditional Medicine Wisdom Bill, and assigned the Subcommittee on Legal Affairs to study in advance the Bill on the Establishment of Labour Courts and Labour Procedure and the Human Trafficking Procedure Bill, under Rule 119 of the Rules of Procedure of the Senate. It noted the work of 3 subcommittees and approved what the Subcommittee on Police Affairs proposed on 6 complaints (1 sent to the Royal Thai Police for consideration within its duties and powers, 3 for which the police units concerned will be invited to provide information, and 2 closed because the agencies have already acted). It noted information on Bangkok's inspection of entertainment venues after the fire on 19 October 2026 (40 venues ordered to stop operating for lack of a licence, and 24 more ordered to stop music and entertainment shows only), and progress of the working groups on technology crime (extended by 30 days) and on drugs (2 report on drug-free communities). Lak Song Metropolitan Police Station was invited to provide information on helping an elderly person avoid being tricked into transferring money, with 1,900,000 baht kept safe, and the meeting resolved to write to the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police to commend this work. The minutes of Meeting No. 26/2569 were approved, and advisers of the committee and subcommittees were changed from 28 October 2026.

Proposals from the Sa Kaeo study visit on helping those affected according to the actual damage, a new road-safety working group, and study visits to Nan, Buri Ram and Surin
se: Meeting on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, at 13.00, Meeting Room 401, Floor 4, Parliament House (the first meeting after the meeting of 29 September 2026 was not held). The meeting noted 3 matters from the Special Committee on Senate Affairs: the Senate's royal Kathin robe offering ceremony on 19 November 2026 at Wat Phakhininat, a request to attend Senate sittings and avoid scheduling committee meetings at the same time, and an invitation to donate to flood victims. It noted the Cabinet resolution extending the period under Section 167 of the National Police Act by 1 more years, and approved a draft amendment to the Criminal Code on detention in place of fines, to allow community service or public-benefit work instead of fines. It resolved to send the proposals from the study visit to Sa Kaeo Province (28 August 2026) to the agencies concerned: to help people affected by the actions of forces from outside the country with the cost of repairing homes, rice barns, farm buildings and animal pens according to the actual damage, without a ceiling. It noted the work of 3 subcommittees, approved a working group under the Subcommittee on Police Affairs to study road safety, tourism and illegal foreign workers (90 days from 21 October 2026), assigned the Subcommittee on Police Affairs to gather information on 1 new complaints, approved study visits to Nan Province (29–31 October 2026) and to Buri Ram–Surin (5–7 November 2026), and approved the report of the seminar summarising the committee's 2 years of work and the report of the study visit to Buri Ram and Surin.

te: Keeping DSI special case files secure and the problem of identity fraud in civil registration, with 3 seminars scheduled
se: The meeting noted Cabinet resolutions and the work of its subcommittees and working groups, and considered 3 petitions (including proposals from the Senators Meet the People project). It considered measures for keeping personal data and evidence in special case files secure after news reports that case documents had been made public; the Department of Special Investigation explained that it has strictly enforced orders to keep case files confidential under the law. It also studied the problem of identity fraud in civil and nationality registration, following news reports that an unusually large number of foreign children's names had been found in house registrations in Din Daeng District, inviting the Department of Provincial Administration and the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration to give information, and scheduled 3 seminars in September

te: Narcotics through airports: the narcotics suppression police and the ONCB invited, and a working group set up on foreign investment and nominees
se: The meeting noted the work of its 3 subcommittees and 3 working groups, including a new working group studying how to promote honest and transparent foreign investment together with measures against nominee structures and evasion of the law. It considered 4 petitions and continued to study the smuggling of narcotics through airports, inviting the Narcotics Suppression Bureau and the Office of the Narcotics Control Board to give information. It received reports on the meeting at Makkasan Metropolitan Police Station (17 Jul) and the study visit to Provincial Police Region 2 and Pattaya Special Prison (20–21 Jul 2026), and scheduled a study visit to Rayong Province on 2–4 Sep 2026
